blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face significant risk despite nothing being criminalised — this country has no anti-LGBT legislation of the type seen in some of its neighbours — and an administrative practice for legal gender recognition exists (medicalised). The national LGBT organisation's 2024 annual report documents ongoing violations including inhuman/degrading treatment, and hate speech is routine in public discourse; the failure of a 2018 anti-discrimination bill means there is still no protection statute covering sexual orientation or gender identity. The capital has a small organised community (the national LGBT organisation and a trans-led one), but visibility carries real risk.

For a visitor: no legal exposure; social hostility significant outside the capital's central districts; police response unreliable.
blindOutOfScope: The missing protection statute and the medicalised legal-gender-recognition practice are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Annual report by an LGBT rights NGO on the human-rights situation of LGBT+ people in this country during 2024. Documents discrimination, torture and inhuman/degrading treatment including sexual violence, domestic violence and extortion targeting LGBT people, violations of private and family life, education and work rights, and hate speech - including a chapter on the pressure around a transgender individual's participation in a beauty pageant.

Crowd-sourced platform data comparing this country with two neighbours: decriminalised here in 2003; legal gender change legal but requires surgery (since 2006); gender-affirming care restricted; no nonbinary recognition; hate-crime protections 'ambiguous' since 2022; no SOGI discrimination protections; same-sex marriage banned. Public-opinion acceptance scores very low (5/100).

Fact-finding mission report on LGBT people in this country (Feb 2009) by a regional LGBT federation and a community organisation: comprehensive coverage of visibility, coming out, societal and institutional homophobia, media coverage, HIV/AIDS, discrimination, harassment and violence, community organising, and legislation affecting LGBT people.

Local LGBT blog archive (May 2012): a neo-fascist arson attack on a gay-friendly do-it-yourself bar in the capital - an improvised incendiary bottle thrown, fire set; police took 12 hours to respond; two suspects identified via CCTV - documents anti-LGBT hate violence in this country.

Foreign broadsheet (April 2019): this country's first registered trans woman received death threats (including lawmakers calling for her to be burned alive) after a historic speech in the national assembly on LGBTI discrimination - documents extreme political hostility toward trans people.
NOTE: this is a foreign government's human-rights landing page at a UN duty station (site navigation only at fetch time); no content specific to this country was retrievable.
blindLocalsOnly: The medicalised legal gender recognition practice and the absence of a SOGI protection statute are resident-facing; a visitor's documents come from their home country.
